name: CA-31
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 8-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Prediction markets price Cisneros at ~95% to win
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Cisneros: an incumbent in a district that leaned Democratic by 8 points, running in a favorable environment, with a roughly nine-to-one fundraising edge over Eric Ching and no outside spending against him. Markets price this race at about 95% Democratic, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Cisneros or a shift in the national House environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gil Cisneros, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election against Republican Eric Ching in a Southern California district that voted about 8 points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles. The national House environment also favors Democrats this cycle, and incumbency adds a further edge.

The resource picture is lopsided: Cisneros has raised about $705,000 with $260,000 on hand, while Ching has raised roughly $82,000, and no outside groups are opposing the incumbent. Prediction markets give Cisneros about a 95% chance of winning. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on these fundamentals, pointing to a comfortable double-digit Democratic win.
